title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup Crock
seoTitle: Loaded Baked Potato Soup Crock | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Creamy potato soup with bacon and cheese toppings
subtitle: Creamy potato soup with bacon and cheese toppings
description: Potatoes, broth, bacon, cheese, and sour cream become thick, comforting soup in the slow cooker.

steps.title: Morning start
steps.instruction: Add peeled potato cubes, broth, onion, and seasonings to the slow cooker.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.instruction: Cook on low for 7 hours until potatoes crush easily against the side with a spoon.

steps.title: Cook bacon
steps.instruction: Bake bacon on lined pans until crisp, then drain it well and crumble after cooling.

steps.title: Mash potatoes
steps.instruction: Mash about half the potatoes in the cooker; leave some chunks for baked-potato texture.

steps.title: Make slurry
steps.instruction: Whisk cornstarch with cold water until smooth so it will not form lumps in soup.

steps.title: Thicken soup
steps.instruction: Stir slurry into simmering soup and cook until it lightly coats a spoon.

steps.title: Add dairy
steps.instruction: Lower heat, then stir in sour cream and cheese gradually so the soup does not split.

steps.title: Check heat
steps.instruction: Warm soup back to 165°F while stirring the bottom to prevent scorching.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Keep the cooker on warm and confirm soup stays above 140°F during service.

steps.title: Load bowls
steps.instruction: Ladle soup and top with bacon, cheddar, green onions, and extra sour cream.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover the soup — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. Keep the reserved garnish sour cream and bacon refrigerated separately from the crock — they get spooned on fresh at serving, not held warm in the pot. On return, bring the soup back to 165°F, stirring gently so it doesn't split, before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Bacon and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Add dairy after potatoes are tender.
Use an immersion blender only for a smoother soup.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Bacon in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Use leftovers as a casserole sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is inexpensive, familiar, and easy to keep hot for a delayed dinner.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: cook bacon and chop potatoes 1 day ahead. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: bring soup to 165°F while stirring.
substitutions: Use Greek yogurt for sour cream.
